## Parties

This Mutual Confidentiality Agreement is entered into by and between Ironbridge Data SARL (the "First Party") and Dunmore Slate Ltd (the "Second Party"), each referred to individually as a "Party" and together as the "Parties". This Agreement takes effect on 13 June 2026 (the "Effective Date") and is entered into in connection with an integration of two products (the "Purpose").

## Confidential Information

"Confidential Information" means any information disclosed by one Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party") in connection with the Purpose, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically or by any other means, and whether or not marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure. Confidential Information includes, without limitation, technical data, product designs, specifications, source code, interface and integration documentation, test results, roadmaps, business plans, pricing, financial information, customer and supplier details, and the existence and contents of the discussions between the Parties regarding the Purpose. Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party; (b) was lawfully in the Receiving Party's possession, free of any obligation of confidence, before disclosure by the Disclosing Party; (c) is lawfully received from a third party who is free to disclose it; or (d) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Confidential Information.

## Obligations

Each Receiving Party shall hold the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence and shall use it solely for the Purpose. The Receiving Party shall not disclose Confidential Information to any third party without the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party, except to its employees, officers, directors, contractors and professional advisers who need to know it for the Purpose and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less protective than those set out here; the Receiving Party remains responsible for their compliance. Disclosure compelled by law, regulation or a competent authority is permitted, provided the Receiving Party gives prompt written notice where lawful and discloses only what is required. On written request, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy the Confidential Information, subject to retention required by law or routine backup.

## Term

This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for a term of 60 months.

## Governing Law

This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or in connection with it are governed by and construed in accordance with the law of France.
